<pasted_content id="6554">
I checked it, and the update prompt does not pop up on its own.
What I did:

1. I quit the installed JusPrin 2.0.0 on your Mac and set `jusprin_update_last_attempt` to `"0"` in its settings file. I saved a copy of the file first at `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/710d8e8d-0d6b-4a8f-9d8f-a3910b8238b8/scratchpad/JusPrin2.conf.before-update-test`. On the Mac this file has no checksum line, so the edit was safe.
2. I started 2.0.0 again. 12 seconds after starting, its log said “JusPrin’s update check: found 2.0.1”.
3. I waited until the app had been running for over a minute, then looked at every window it had.

What I saw:

* The app showed only its usual windows. No update dialog or prompt opened.
* Home looks exactly as it did before the check. The gear icon at the top right has no dot or badge either.
* The update shows up only if someone opens Preferences and looks: a dot beside “Updates”, and on that page the “JusPrin 2.0.1 is available” card. This matches the code, where the Preferences window is the only part of the app that receives the update check’s result.

So someone on 2.0.0 who never opens Preferences won’t learn that 2.0.1 exists. The app ran the new check itself and saved its normal settings, so there’s nothing to restore. 2.0.0 is still running.
</pasted_content id="6554">

investigate why

Rules that follow:

- **No pill is the all-clear, and it is never given before a check.** The pill is drawn only while OrcaSlicer reports an issue, ignored ones included. While OrcaSlicer holds an unapplied edit the last issues are kept, the pill says it is checking and both buttons are off, so the pill does not go until OrcaSlicer has looked. An issue that was not in the list before is announced once by a ring that spreads from the pill twice; an edit that keeps an issue, and ignoring one or undoing that, announce nothing.
- **Nothing is resolved by the fork.** An issue goes when OrcaSlicer lets go of its notification. An agent saying it fixed something changes nothing.
- **"Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's answer.** An error-level notification blocks. For the slice result it is OrcaSlicer's own post-slice check, which allows a path 2 mm past the plate edge; the monitor does not apply a stricter test of its own.
- **The object is never read out of the words.** Two messages of one kind are told apart by comparing OrcaSlicer's words now with its words before, as OrcaSlicer does itself. Which object a message is about always comes from a check's own ids.
- **A press acts on what is true at the press**, and with no assistant set up it sends nothing and offers the chat panel's setup. **One button, one question**: Ask AI sends "Explain this issue and my options." with the issue as context, and the turn gets the ordinary tools, so the person asks for a fix in the chat. A second "Resolve with AI" button was removed on 2026-10-28: it sent the same context with the same tools and differed only in the sentence, which the person could not tell apart.
- **Slice-result warnings follow OrcaSlicer's send dialog.** The warnings the G-code processor stores on a slice result (bed temperature, nozzle hardness, timelapse) are shown as OrcaSlicer's Bambu send dialog shows them, the only place OrcaSlicer itself shows them: never the bed-temperature one, the traditional-timelapse one once although it is stored twice. The chip and `slice_report` read one fork-owned table, `Workspace/SliceResultWarnings`, whose comment says why it is a copy and not an upstream seam, and a guard test fails when OrcaSlicer defines a kind the table does not classify. The timelapse ones apply only to a print that records a timelapse, which is chosen when it is sent: `slice_report` and Check print list them marked so, and the chip does not count them.
- **Operation failures are not print issues.** A failed download or a refused arrange is a confirmation, never an entry in the issue list.
- **Closing hides, it never resolves.** The pill is always there and is the way back; the list and the bubble are opened and closed, one at a time, and closing either changes nothing about the issue or the count. The list closes on a pick, a second press of the pill, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to the selection: opening it selects its object, and it closes when that object stops being selected, which is what a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do in OrcaSlicer. Turning the view or dragging the object leaves it open. Its close button leaves the selection alone, and a press on **Ask AI** that reaches the chat closes it. With one issue the pill opens the bubble directly, and with several the bubble's pager walks them all. The overlay hears Escape and presses through handlers of its own on the canvas's window, bound after OrcaSlicer's and so called first; no OrcaSlicer file is involved.
- **Ignoring a warning is the person's mark, not OrcaSlicer's.** **Ignore this warning** in the bubble leaves OrcaSlicer's notification alone: the warning stays in the list, marked, below the ones that count, and the pill stops counting it ("1 warning ignored" when nothing else is left, never "No print issues"). Only a warning can be ignored; a blocker cannot, because OrcaSlicer would still refuse to print. An ignore lasts while OrcaSlicer keeps reporting that warning on the active plate's own list, and is forgotten when OrcaSlicer stops, so a warning that comes back is shown again. It is not saved with the project. The rule is `mark_ignored` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue`.

Known limits: application and account notifications (update available, plug-in missing, preset sync conflict) are routed to `App` and drawn nowhere yet. A confirmation shows OrcaSlicer's words and a close button; the actions OrcaSlicer attached to its own notification (open folder, eject, cancel an upload) are not offered. Only a slice has a percentage and a known ending; other work shows a bar with no amount and is recorded as done unless its Cancel was pressed. Uploads and downloads have not been run. The tips and the object size card are not shown.

### Agent WebView

The production Agent interface is a separate React/TypeScript package that runs locally inside a `wxWebView`. It needs:

- a versioned schema for commands and events;
- scripted mock conversations that play back the same way every time, for UI tests;
127:Print again sends a recorded G-code's kept file, never a fresh slice, and always through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog, where the person presses Send. A Bambu printer takes a `.gcode.3mf`, so a Bambu print also keeps the package it uploaded (`<hash>.gcode.3mf`, and for a cloud printer the config 3MF it also sent), byte for byte, with its SHA-256 on the send (`packageHash`); it goes when its G-code's copy is pruned. Print again parses that package, hands it to Select Machine through `Plater::update_print_required_data` and `EVT_PRINT_FROM_SDCARD_VIEW` (the printer file browser's print-from-storage mode, which draws the plate, picture and filaments from the file), and sets the dialog's new-print flag (`SelectMachineDialog::set_required_data_new_print`, the one upstream seam), so the job uploads the local file as a new print instead of asking the printer to print by name. Printing from the printer's storage is not used: the file name on the printer is reused per project, so it cannot say which version would print. A print host with OrcaSlicer's standard upload dialog is sent a temporary copy of the kept G-code (the queue deletes what it uploads); ElegooLink, Creality Print, Flashforge's local API and `use_3mf` hosts are not offered Print again. `GcodeHistoryRecorder::print_again_state` decides whether it is offered for the printer selected now; a kept file whose hash no longer matches is never sent and the entry says so. `print_dialog_open` opens the same dialogs for the agent: a plate's slice, or with `gcode` a recorded G-code.

The chat panel opens when work starts. Repeats are folded by the page, never in what is saved, and an entry still "running" in a project that was closed mid-run reads as interrupted. |

input.ask: Should JusPrin tell people about a new version outside Preferences?

content.text:
The update check works. JusPrin 2.0.0 never pops up a prompt because it was designed that way: the result only ever appears in Preferences › Updates. I changed nothing.

**What the code does.** In [UpdateCheck.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp), the app checks GitHub 10 seconds after it starts, then again every hour. A check only runs if the last successful one was more than a day ago. When the check finds a newer version it saves it to the settings file and tells whoever is listening. Only one part of the app listens: the Preferences window ([PreferencesWindow.cpp:186](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp:186)). That window draws the dot beside "Updates" and the "JusPrin 2.0.1 is available" card. Home, the project screen, the gear icon and the chat never hear about it. Before JusPrin, OrcaSlicer had its own "new version" window that opened at startup. JusPrin turned that check off on purpose so OrcaSlicer's server is never asked ([ShellController.cpp:2094](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:2094)). So nothing else shows an update either.

**Where the design came from.** The JusPrin v2 design canvas has a note dated 2026-10-22 next to the Updates boards. It says the result shows "only here, plus the dot on Updates". It also says "Nothing pops up, and nothing appears in a project or in chat." The commit that added the check, 80ed1692ff on 2026-10-23, follows that note. I couldn't find your own words behind it: the session where it was decided isn't in the searchable transcripts. So it's unverified whether you chose "no pop-up" yourself or it was a proposal that got written down as decided.

**What this means for people already on 2.0.0.** Anything we change now only ships in a later release. People running 2.0.0 or 2.0.1 keep today's behaviour until they update by hand. Inside the app there's one other way to reach them. The server can refuse an old version, and the app then shows a "Get the new version…" button on the chat, sign-in and model picker. But that blocks their account, so it only makes sense when an old version really has to stop working. For the people on 2.0.0 now, the realistic routes are outside the app: an email, or a post where they already follow JusPrin.

**Decision needed: should JusPrin tell people about a new version anywhere besides Preferences?** It's your call because it changes what people see on screens outside Preferences, and the current design says nothing pops up.
- **Keep it as is.** Costs nothing. Most people will never find out a new version exists.
- **Put a dot on the gear icon on Home and on the project screen.** Small and quiet, about a day of work. It's still easy to miss, because the dot doesn't say what it means.
- **Show a one-line notice on Home once per new version.** For example: "JusPrin 2.0.1 is available", with Download and Skip buttons. It never appears inside a project or during a print. About a day or two of work plus new design boards. People can't miss it, and they can dismiss it.

My pick is the once-per-version notice on Home. If you agree, I'll draw the boards on the canvas first and build after you've seen them.
Yes, design a notice

result.output: # JusPrin design guidelines **Status:** Canonical guidance for `jusprin-dev` on how a screen gets designed and checked, and on the words it shows. The visual system (tokens, type, color, components, logo) lives in [Design system](design-system.md); this document does not repeat it. Design agents tend to write on-screen text that only they can read. The agent knows how the screen works, so a line like "The sixth digit signs you in." reads clearly to it and to any reviewer who knows the same. A person opening the app for the first time has to decode it, and often can't. The First-Launch Confusion Review (https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15, 2026-11-06) found 23 places on the first launch where a newcomer would misread or stall, and most of them were wording. The rules below exist to stop that at the source and to catch what still gets through. ## How a screen gets designed and checked These steps apply to every change to text a person sees, not only to new screens: a new link on an existing board, a reworded line, or a one-sentence fix all get the cold-reader check on the board before building (step 5) and in the running app after (step 8). 1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those. 2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says. 3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board. 4. **Write every line by the wording rule below.** 5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended. 6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer. 7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code). 8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads. ## The cold-reader check The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works. - Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything. - Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see. - Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out. - Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders. What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test. ## Wording Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has. The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app. 1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses. - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had) - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it 2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for. - Before: "New or existing account, same door." - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent) - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice." 3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside. - Before: "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device." - After: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone." 4. **Internal labels.** A name the team uses, shown nowhere else on the screen, explains nothing. - Before: "An Expert message is 5 credits." - After: the cost in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent" (check the number against real costs) 5. **Hinting at a consequence instead of stating it.** If a choice changes what the person gets, say what it changes. - Before: "Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours." - After: "If you skip, files are sliced for a stand-in printer with a 250 mm bed, not for yours. Add your printer before you print anything. You can do that later on the home screen." Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening. --- name: canvas-boards-from-bundle-rules description: "Kenneth's 2026-10-21 correction: a canvas board I draw must copy the Design System bundle's CSS rules and the app's own markup, never an older board or memory; the calibration page had 14 px menu rows drawn at 13, a missing Connect… row, a black Remove, a stale reply-choice style and more." metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback originSessionId: 9ce2f3c8-7b6d-4ba7-99ce-889f9d9f192a modified: 2026-10-22T00:09:35.890Z --- Kenneth, 2026-10-21, on the calibration page I drew: "It looks like you didn't follow this hygiene. read design guidelines in readme, and fix your own sloppiness", then "I suspect there were more sloppiness in the boards you designed". import functools, http.server, json, re, socketserver, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading
from pathlib import Path
args = sys.argv[1:]
dark = '--dark' in args
if dark: args.remove('--dark')
work, out, names = Path(args[0]), Path(args[1]), args[2:]
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
proj, runtime = work / 'project', work / 'runtime'
blobs = json.loads((runtime / 'blobs.json').read_text()) if (runtime / 'blobs.json').exists() else {}
chrome = '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'
class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def translate_path(self, path):
        p = path.split('?')[0]
        if p.endswith('/support.js'): return str(runtime / 'dc-runtime.js')
        if p.startswith('/_blob/'):
            b = blobs.get(p[7:])
            if b: return str(runtime / b)
        return super().translate_path(path)

input.ask: Should I build the new-version card as drawn?

content.text:
I've drawn the notice. When a new version is out, a card appears at the top of Home's right column, above Printers. It's on the [JusPrin v2 canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ#page-updating), page "Updating JusPrin", as boards 07 (light) and 08 (dark), and both are marked as a proposal. No code is written yet.

**What the card says** (the picture is attached above):
- **JusPrin 2.0.1 is available**
- "You have version 2.0.0. Your projects, printers and settings stay when you install the new one. Installing doesn't affect a print your printer is already running."
- **See what's new**: opens Preferences › Updates, which already shows the release notes.
- "The download page is on GitHub. Pick the file for your computer there: Mac, Windows or Linux."
- **Open download page ↗**: opens the GitHub release page, like Download in Preferences. The card stays until the new version is running.
- **Remind me tomorrow**: hides the card for 24 hours.
- **Skip this version**: works the same as Skip in Preferences. The card goes away, and it comes back when a newer release is out.

It never shows inside a project, in a chat or as a separate window. There's no card for a Microsoft Store install, or when automatic checks are off or stealth mode is on.

**What the wording checks changed.** Three fresh readers saw only the screenshot. The first draft quoted the opening line of the release notes. The reader didn't know "the printer chat" or what "languages that write decimals with a comma" meant, and those notes are in English only while the app now runs in 22 languages, so that line came out. Readers also hesitated in four other places:
- They expected "Download" to download a file, so it's now "Open download page".
- "Skip this version" was the only way to close the card and it sounded permanent, so I added "Remind me tomorrow".
- "Remind me later" didn't say when, which is why it now says tomorrow.
- One reader worried that installing would stop the print running on their printer, so the card now says it won't.

The third reader understood every line and all three buttons as intended. What they still wondered about (which file to pick, how to install) is answered on the GitHub release page itself.

**Still open:**
- The card promises that a running print keeps going while JusPrin is quit and reinstalled. I believe that's true for every connection type, because the printer runs the job on its own, but I haven't tested it. It should be checked before building.
- Anything built now only reaches people once they're on the release that contains it. People on 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 will never see this card, so reaching them needs an email or a post.

**Other canvas changes:**
- The Preferences note from 2026-10-22 that says "Nothing pops up" now has a line saying this proposal would replace that rule if you agree.
- No existing board needed marking as superseded, because the Home boards without the card still show Home when JusPrin is up to date.
How difficult is it to have the updates automatically happen instead of asking the user to download and manually run the update?

input.ask: Which update path should JusPrin take?

content.text:
It's moderately hard. With a full "Install and restart" button, I estimate two to three weeks of work, and most of the risk is on Windows. A smaller version, where the app downloads the installer and opens it for the person, would take a few days. Both figures are my estimates, not measurements.

**What JusPrin ships today**

- **Mac:** a signed and notarised disk image, so Apple accepts it as coming from us.
- **Windows:** an unsigned installer, plus a zip that runs without installing.
- **Linux:** an AppImage, a single file that runs as is.

OrcaSlicer has no in-app installer either, so there's nothing upstream to reuse.

**What "install and restart" takes on each platform**

- **Mac, about 3–5 days.** Sparkle is the standard tool for this. It downloads the update, checks it, swaps the app in place and relaunches. We would add Sparkle to the app bundle and keep a private signing key in the release workflow. Each release then signs its disk image and publishes a small list of versions for the app to read. The signing step needs care: Sparkle's helper programs must be signed one by one before the app itself ([Sparkle's publishing docs](https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/publishing/), [one developer's write-up of the pitfalls](https://steipete.me/posts/2025/code-signing-and-notarization-sparkle-and-tears)).
- **Windows, about 3–5 days, plus a decision for you.** WinSparkle, or our own code, would download the installer, check its signature, close JusPrin and run the installer silently. Our installer accepts the standard silent switch, `/S`. The catch is that our installer is unsigned. Having the app download and run an unsigned program on its own is the riskiest part of the whole plan, so the app must at least check a signature of our own on every download. Antivirus programs may also flag it. I haven't confirmed whether Windows' download warning (SmartScreen) fires for an installer the app downloads itself, so that has to be tested. Buying a Windows code-signing certificate removes most of this risk.
- **Linux, about 2–3 days.** AppImage has its own update mechanism, AppImageUpdate, which downloads only the parts of the file that changed ([AppImage docs](https://docs.appimage.org/packaging-guide/optional/updates.html)).

**What auto-update can't reach**

- People already on 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 must install the next version by hand once.
- The Windows zip and Microsoft Store installs can't update themselves. Store installs get updates from the Store anyway.
- A bug in the updater can strand people on that version, so each release needs a test of updating from the previous one.

**The smaller version.** PrusaSlicer does this in [its updater](https://github.com/prusa3d/PrusaSlicer/blob/master/src/slic3r/Utils/AppUpdater.cpp). It downloads the file inside the app. On Windows it runs the installer, and on Mac it opens the disk image in Finder for the person to drag across. On Linux it only downloads the file. That saves the trip to GitHub, but on Mac people still drag the app themselves. One person on Prusa's forum reported that the Mac update didn't replace the old app ([forum thread](https://forum.prusa3d.com/forum/prusaslicer/problems-with-automatic-update)).

**Decision needed: should JusPrin install updates itself, or only download them?**
- **Install and restart.** About two to three weeks, plus a Windows code-signing certificate if you want the Windows side safe and free of warnings. The card on Home would then offer "Install and restart" instead of "Open download page".
- **Download in the app only.** A few days. The person still runs the installer or drags the app, as today, just without visiting GitHub.
- **Keep the current card.** No extra work. People keep downloading from GitHub themselves.

My pick is Install and restart, built Mac first with Sparkle because that path is the most proven, and Windows only once the signing question is settled. Either way the card on Home is still needed, and only its buttons change.

Three points need your call before it can be: the offline message, the Linux file replacement, and saving before quitting. The Windows install-and-restart prototype session is still running.

content.text:
The new-version card for Home is now on the canvas, redrawn so that JusPrin downloads the update itself. It's on the "Updating JusPrin" page at https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ#page-updating, boards 07 to 15. Nothing is built yet. These are proposals for you to approve.

**What the person sees, step by step**
- **Card appears:** when the update check finds 2.0.1, a card shows at the top of Home's right column. It offers Download, Remind me tomorrow and Skip this version.
- **Downloading:** pressing Download saves the file to the Downloads folder while they keep working. The card shows "212 MB of 475 MB" with a Cancel button. If JusPrin quits mid-download, the download starts over next time.
- **Download finished:** the card's button saves unsaved changes and quits JusPrin. Then:
  - **Mac:** it opens the disk image. The disk image window itself says what to do: drag JusPrin onto Applications, choose Replace, then open JusPrin from the Dock. It has to work this way because I checked on this Mac that Finder refuses to replace an app that's running.
  - **Windows:** it runs the installer, and the person opens JusPrin from the Start menu afterwards.
  - **Linux:** it puts 2.0.1 in place of the running AppImage and starts it.
- **After updating:** the first time 2.0.1 opens, the card says "You're now on JusPrin 2.0.1" and offers to move the installer to the Trash.
- **Connection lost:** if the download stops because the connection dropped, the card says so and offers Try again.

**Cold-reader checks.** Fresh agents read only the screenshots, three times. I fixed what they misread. For example, "your current JusPrin file" on Linux sounded like it would overwrite a project, and "Replace" on the Mac sounded like it would delete projects.

**Decision needed: the offline message.** Board 13 tells the person "Your computer lost its internet connection. Check it, then try again." Under the error-handling rules, a message of its own counts as an expected error, and each one needs your yes. Every other download failure would get the usual "Something went wrong on our side" message and a report. My pick is to approve it, because checking the connection is something the person can actually do. The box below asks it.

**Decision needed: Linux goes one step past "download only".** If JusPrin only downloaded the new AppImage, the person's menu and desktop shortcuts would keep opening 2.0.0. The options:
- **Do nothing more:** the person has to replace the file by hand, and most won't know they need to.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

# JusPrin's translations

JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for
(`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's
catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own
text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never
conflicts in a translation file:

| Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL`, `translated_plural` | `native/<lang>.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`, the catalog the app loads |
| The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/<lang>.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) |

Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of
`native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used.

## Updating the catalogs

After marking or changing text:

```bash
python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py
```

It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the
pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new
entry in every `<lang>.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's
`AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line
break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine
translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: <what>` where
the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails
while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder.

The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like
`<0>…</0>` for elements inside a `Trans`, and
`{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the
placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a
plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses
(`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`).

## Marking text

Mark every string a person reads: labels, buttons, headings, menu items,
tooltips, `aria-label`s, placeholders, empty states, confirmation and error
text. Do not change the English: marking must leave the source text exactly
as it was.

Leave these in English, unmarked:

- **Text the AI model reads**: prompts, skills, tool descriptions and tool
  results, the project and printer instructions, anything that goes into a
  request to a model. The model speaks the person's language on its own, and
  `wording.test.ts` guards that text. When the same string is shown to the
  person and also sent to the model, translate it only where it is shown.
- Identifiers and values the code compares, protocol fields, CSS classes,
  test ids, file names, URLs, setting keys, G-code.
- Log lines and the text of error reports (`report_unexpected`,
  `report_error`): they are read by developers.
- Names: JusPrin, OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, printer and filament model names.

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject
`<script>` right after `<head>` that (1) defines `window.wx` answering `hello` with
`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.

`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming
activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

# JusPrin guide

How to use JusPrin, one page per part of the app. The same pages are in the app, under Help › JusPrin guide…, in the order of the list below.

- [Projects and files](projects-and-files.md)
- [Plates and objects](plates-and-objects.md)
- [Printers and filament](printers-and-filament.md)
- [Seeing and changing print settings](print-settings.md)
- [Slicing, checking and printing](slicing-and-printing.md)
- [AI chats, account and credits](ai-chats-and-account.md)
- [The app itself](the-app.md)

## Before a release

The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.

1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
3. Fix what it reports, then run it again until it passes:
   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
   - **AI answered a question wrongly.** Read its reply in the output. Usually the page is unclear or its first line does not say when to read it.
4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.
5. Commit the pages together with their pictures, the skills the command rebuilt, and `checked-version.txt`. When every step passes for every page, the command writes the app's version to that file. A run with `--skip-app`, with `--area`, or without `--ask-ai` leaves it as it was. The release workflow refuses a version this file does not name. The file says the check passed for that version, not on which commit, so run it on the commit you mean to release.

## What the command does

1. **Walks the app and takes the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that go through the screens the page describes, and the checks in each run the page depends on. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them in the app as built and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`.
2. **Rebuilds the copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from each page.
3. **Checks each page**, in `guide.test.ts` beside it: every label in bold is in the app's source, every section has a run in step 1, every picture is one step 1 took, and the page has questions for step 4. `components/Guide.test.tsx` checks that the app's guide window lists every page and shows each with all its pictures and without the parts written for AI.
4. **Asks AI the page's questions** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds them with what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.

## Writing a page

- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it. The model reads every page's description together in one list, and the Claude command-line tool that `--ask-ai` runs through cuts a tool description longer than about 2,000 characters, so keep each one short: about 200 bytes. Write `...` rather than `…` in it, since that tool rewrites the one as the other.
- Put words that are only for AI in `<!-- ai: … -->`. They are hidden on this site.
- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
- A picture goes on a line of its own, as `![what it shows](pictures/<page>/<name>.png)`, and comes from a run named in `guide_checks.json`. AI's copy leaves it out.
- A picture is kept at twice the screen's size, and the guide window shows it at half, the size it has on screen. Mark a run's picture that the harness draws at the screen's own size with `"atScreenSize": true`, and the command doubles it.
- List a new page at the top of this file, or the guide window leaves it out.
- Give each `##` section a run in `guide_checks.json`.
- Add at least three questions for the page to `guide_questions.json`.
- AI's copy may hold at most 16 KiB. Split a page that grows past that.

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

   - **JusPrin's update check:**
     - `Updates::UpdateCheck` and `UpdateRecord`, with settings in AppConfig: `jusprin_update_*` keys and `kFeedUrlKey` = "jusprin_update_feed_url", used to point tests at a local server.

     - `HomeHost` handles the page's messages and pushes `state` with `state_payload(Snapshot)`.

     - `HomeWebView` runs a poll timer (100 ms) and a live timer (1 s).
     - `HomeHost::poll` calls `poll_onboarding`.

     ```cpp
     void remind_later(AppConfig& config, std::time_t until) { config.set(kRemindKey, std::to_string(until)); }
     std::optional<Release> home_notice(const AppConfig& config, const std::string& running, std::time_t now)
     {
         if (!auto_check_enabled(config) || config.get_bool("stealth_mode"))
             return std::nullopt;
         // A clock set back by more than a day must not hide the card for longer.
         const std::time_t remind = read_time(config, kRemindKey);

             return std::nullopt;
         return load_record(config, running).available;
     }
     ```

     ```cpp
     void UpdateCheck::remind_later() { Updates::remind_later(config(), now() + 24 * 60 * 60); notify(); }
     std::optional<Release> UpdateCheck::home_notice() const {
     ```

# Windows "install and restart" prototype: what happened on the VM

Measured 2026-11-19 on the GCP Windows test VM (jusprin-win-test, Windows Server 2022, no GPU).
It started from JusPrin 2.0.0 installed in C:\Program Files\JusPrin and the real %APPDATA%\JusPrin2 data folder,
which has 4 projects, an Anker M5 printer and an Anthropic API key. Nothing was committed or landed.
The test program is updater_proto.cpp in this folder. It compiles the app's own src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp
against the deps on the VM (build.cmd). The test scripts are common.ps1 and c1/c2/c3.ps1, and helper-log.txt is its log.

## Measured

- Download: `Slic3r::Http::get(<release url>)` fetched the 192 MB installer in 3.2 s. That is GCP bandwidth; a home connection will be slower.
  Checking it against SHA256SUMS.txt took 3.4 s and the sums matched.
- The downloaded file has no Zone.Identifier stream (no "downloaded from the internet" mark).
- From a normal-user process (medium integrity, started through Explorer):
  - `CreateProcessW("<installer> /S")` fails with error 740 (requires elevation). The installer's manifest says `requireAdministrator`.
  - `ShellExecuteExW(verb "open", "<installer>", "/S")` shows the UAC prompt (consent.exe). No SmartScreen step runs first.
    The prompt is on the secure desktop, so my screenshot tool could not capture it ("The handle is invalid").
- The same file with Edge's mark (ZoneId=3), opened from Explorer, shows SmartScreen's "Windows protected your PC"; "More info" shows
  "Publisher: Unknown publisher" plus "Run anyway". Downloading it in Edge first shows "isn't commonly downloaded. Make sure you trust …".
  For the double-click test I wrote Edge's mark onto a copy myself, because Edge's download panel ignored synthetic clicks.
- Defender reported no detections (Get-MpThreatDetection was empty).
- `/S` works. Fresh install: 33 s, exit 0. It installs per-machine to C:\Program Files\JusPrin, uninstall key HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\…\Uninstall\JusPrin.

input.description: Find my earlier answer on automatic updates in this session's transcript

result.output:
It's moderately hard. With a full "Install and restart" button, I estimate two to three weeks of work, and most of the risk is on Windows. A smaller version, where the app downloads the installer and opens it for the person, would take a few days. Both figures are my estimates, not measurements.

**What JusPrin ships today**

- **Mac:** a signed and notarised disk image, so Apple accepts it as coming from us.
- **Windows:** an unsigned installer, plus a zip that runs without installing.
- **Linux:** an AppImage, a single file that runs as is.

OrcaSlicer has no in-app installer either, so there's nothing upstream to reuse.

**What "install and restart" takes on each platform**

- **Mac, about 3–5 days.** Sparkle is the standard tool for this. It downloads the update, checks it, swaps the app in place and relaunches. We would add Sparkle to the app bundle and keep a private signing key in the release workflow. Each release then signs its disk image and publishes a small list of versions for the app to read. The signing step needs care: Sparkle's helper programs must be signed one by one before the app itself ([Sparkle's publishing docs](https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/publishing/), [one developer's write-up of the pitfalls](https://steipete.me/posts/2025/code-signing-and-notarization-sparkle-and-tears)).
- **Windows, about 3–5 days, plus a decision for you.** WinSparkle, or our own code, would download the installer, check its signature, close JusPrin and run the installer silently. Our installer accepts the standard silent switch, `/S`. The catch is that our installer is unsigned. Having the app download and run an unsigned program on its own is the riskiest part of the whole plan, so the app must at least check a signature of our own on every download. Antivirus programs may also flag it. I haven't confirmed whether Windows' download warning (SmartScreen) fires for an installer the app downloads itself, so that has to be tested. Buying a Windows code-signing certificate removes most of this risk.
- **Linux, about 2–3 days.** AppImage has its own update mechanism, AppImageUpdate, which downloads only the parts of the file that changed ([AppImage docs](https://docs.appimage.org/packaging-guide/optional/updates.html)).

**What auto-update can't reach**

- People already on 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 must install the next version by hand once.
- The Windows zip and Microsoft Store installs can't update themselves. Store installs get updates from the Store anyway.
- A bug in the updater can strand people on that version, so each release needs a test of updating from the previous one.

**The smaller version.** PrusaSlicer does this in [its updater](https://github.com/prusa3d/PrusaSlicer/blob/master/src/slic3r/Utils/AppUpdater.cpp). It downloads the file inside the app. On Windows it runs the installer, and on Mac it opens the disk image in Finder for the person to drag across. On Linux it only downloads the file. That saves the trip to GitHub, but on Mac people still drag the app themselves. One person on Prusa's forum reported that the Mac update didn't replace the old app ([forum thread](https://forum.prusa3d.com/forum/prusaslicer/problems-with-automatic-update)).

**Decision needed: should JusPrin install updates itself, or only download them?**
- **Install and restart.** About two to three weeks, plus a Windows code-signing certificate if you want the Windows side safe and free of warnings. The card on Home would then offer "Install and restart" instead of "Open download page".
- **Download in the app only.** A few days. The person still runs the installer or drags the app, as today, just without visiting GitHub.
- **Keep the current card.** No extra work. People keep downloading from GitHub themselves.

My pick is Install and restart, built Mac first with Sparkle because that path is the most proven, and Windows only once the signing question is settled. Either way the card on Home is still needed, and only its buttons change.
=====
The new-version card for Home is now on the canvas, redrawn so that JusPrin downloads the update itself. It's on the "Updating JusPrin" page at https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ#page-updating, boards 07 to 15. Nothing is built yet. These are proposals for you to approve.

**What the person sees, step by step**
- **Card appears:** when the update check finds 2.0.1, a card shows at the top of Home's right column. It offers Download, Remind me tomorrow and Skip this version.
- **Downloading:** pressing Download saves the file to the Downloads folder while they keep working. The card shows "212 MB of 475 MB" with a Cancel button. If JusPrin quits mid-download, the download starts over next time.
- **Download finished:** the card's button saves unsaved changes and quits JusPrin. Then:
  - **Mac:** it opens the disk image. The disk image window itself says what to do: drag JusPrin onto Applications, choose Replace, then open JusPrin from the Dock. It has to work this way because I checked on this Mac that Finder refuses to replace an app that's running.
  - **Windows:** it runs the installer, and the person opens JusPrin from the Start menu afterwards.
  - **Linux:** it puts 2.0.1 in place of the running AppImage and starts it.
- **After updating:** the first time 2.0.1 opens, the card says "You're now on JusPrin 2.0.1" and offers to move the installer to the Trash.
- **Connection lost:** if the download stops because the connection dropped, the card says so and offers Try again.

**Cold-reader checks.** Fresh agents read only the screenshots, three times. I fixed what they misread. For example, "your current JusPrin file" on Linux sounded like it would overwrite a project, and "Replace" on the Mac sounded like it would delete projects.

**Decision needed: the offline message.** Board 13 tells the person "Your computer lost its internet connection. Check it, then try again." Under the error-handling rules, a message of its own counts as an expected error, and each one needs your yes. Every other download failure would get the usual "Something went wrong on our side" message and a report. My pick is to approve it, because checking the connection is something the person can actually do. The box below asks it.

**Decision needed: Linux goes one step past "download only".** If JusPrin only downloaded the new AppImage, the person's menu and desktop shortcuts would keep opening 2.0.0. The options:
- **Do nothing more:** the person has to replace the file by hand, and most won't know they need to.
- **Rename the new file over the running one, then start it:** a few lines of code, and safe on Linux because the running copy keeps its file open.

My pick is the rename. Do you agree that JusPrin should replace the AppImage on Linux?

**Decision needed: save before quitting.** The cards promise that unsaved changes are kept when JusPrin quits to install. I haven't checked that quitting saves the open project today. The proposal is that the button calls autosave's save-now first. The alternative is to drop the promise from the card. A worried reader asked about exactly this, so my pick is to save first. Should the install button save the open project before quitting?

**Not verified yet**
- A running print keeps going while JusPrin is quit and reinstalled, for every connection type.
- Whether a file JusPrin downloads itself triggers a Gatekeeper or SmartScreen warning. [Prototype Windows install-and-restart on the VM](#local_dd7ca455-eee4-4e50-8ebf-f8bf1b869b32) is measuring this on Windows and is still running. Its branch starts from `main`, so I'll check what it reports before passing it on.

The card reaches people only from the first release that includes it. 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 will never show it.
=====

The search turned up the core architecture, but nothing that shows a silent or fully programmatic install path.

- **Architecture:** The SPUUserDriver protocol is used for implementing a user interface for the Sparkle updater. To build one, you write a class that conforms to the protocol and then create a SPUUpdater with your user driver instead of creating the typical SPUStandardUpdaterController. SPUUpdater and its delegate SPUUpdaterDelegate do not contain any user-interface or AppKit logic.
- **Install behavior:** The docs say the protocol is not used in a way that eliminates UI or installs updates silently. Your UI also needs to let the user be in control of installing an update once an update is found, since installs can trigger an authorization prompt.
- **Authorization:** If the state.stage is SPUUpdateStateNotDownloaded or SPUUpdateStateDownloaded the user may be presented an authorization prompt to install the update when authorization is required, for example if the update is a package install.
- **Focus method:** To support bringing an update back into focus, implement -[SPUUserDriver showUpdateInFocus]. This method used to be required but is now optional since Sparkle 2.8.
- **Build option:** A developer writing their own updater user interface may choose to build Sparkle with SPARKLE_BUILD_UI_BITS=0 which strips out the standard UI bits.
- **Reference implementations:** The repo includes SUPopUpTitlebarUserDriver: Alternative user interface to the Sparkle Test App and SUCommandLineUserDriver: User interface to the sparkle-cli tool, which are useful examples.

**Gap:** None of the results gave the specific method names for triggering an install from code, such as the calls for checking for updates or confirming an install. For those, check the SPUUpdater and SPUUserDriver API reference pages and the Sparkle 2 repo's Test App source.

content.text:
"Install and restart" is feasible. On Windows the prototype has now done the whole flow with your click, and nothing in it blocks a real build. I estimate three to four weeks for all three platforms, up from my earlier two to three. The Windows run turned up work I hadn't counted, and the Mac side hasn't been prototyped yet, so it carries the most uncertainty. These are my estimates, not measurements.

**What the Windows prototype showed on the test VM**
- **The full run.** You clicked Download in Preferences. JusPrin downloaded the 192 MB installer in 9 s and checked it against the release's checksum file. It then asked for administrator rights once and closed. A small helper program ran the installer silently and reopened JusPrin 2.0.1. The new window appeared 69 s after your click. Projects, the printer, the API key and settings were all unchanged, and the reopened app was not running as administrator.
- **SmartScreen.** No "Windows protected your PC" warning appeared. Windows only shows it for files a browser marks as downloaded, and the app's own download carries no mark. The admin prompt still says "Unknown publisher" on every update, because our installer is unsigned.
- **Hazards that real code must handle:**
  - If the installer runs while JusPrin is still open, it reports success but leaves old program files beside new ones. The helper avoids this by waiting until JusPrin has exited.
  - When the disk filled up, the installer stopped halfway. It left a broken folder and no uninstall entry.
  - Install time on the VM varied from 41 s to 136 s.
- **Progress window.** You chose for the helper to draw its own progress window while the app is closed. The bar currently stops at 92% because it compares against the old version's size.

**What the real version needs, per platform**
- **Windows, about 6–8 days.**
  - Build the helper and ship it inside the installer.
  - Save the download to a file instead of memory.
  - Before quitting, check free disk space, check for a second JusPrin window or an upload still being sent to a printer, and save the open project. JusPrin already has project autosave to reuse.
  - Have the release publish the installed size, so the bar fills correctly.
  - Report a helper failure on the next start. The helper runs while JusPrin is closed, so it can't use the app's own error report.
  - Run an end-to-end test on the VM.
- **Mac, about 5–8 days, untested.** Sparkle, the standard Mac updater, swaps the app and relaunches it. To keep the Home card as the only update screen, we'd give Sparkle our own interface, which Sparkle supports ([custom interfaces](https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/custom-user-interfaces/), [SPUUserDriver](https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/api-reference/Protocols/SPUUserDriver.html)). The release workflow would also need a Sparkle signing key, a list of versions for the app to read, and a separate signature on Sparkle's own helper programs.
- **Linux, 1–2 days.** Put the new AppImage file in place of the running one, then start it.
- **All platforms, about 2 days.** New design boards for the card, a cold-reader check of them, and translations.

**Limits that stay whatever we build**
- People on 2.0.0 or 2.0.1, and on the release that first ships this, still update by hand once. Automatic installs start with the release after that.
- Every release needs a test of updating from the previous version. A broken updater strands people on that version.

**Decision needed: should we buy a Windows code-signing certificate?** Without one, every Windows update shows "Unknown publisher" on the admin prompt, and the first download from the website keeps SmartScreen's warning. Microsoft's Azure Artifact Signing is listed from $9.99 a month. Regular certificates cost about $219 a year ([Microsoft's signing options](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/code-signing-options), [price comparison](https://sslinsights.com/best-code-signing-certificate-windows-applications/)). Neither removes SmartScreen right away, because Microsoft builds trust per file over time. My pick is Azure Artifact Signing, if your country is eligible. Should we buy one?

The Windows test build is still installed on the VM, and the prototype branch hasn't been pushed, as you asked.
